## What this section covers

This section covers the understanding of *why* livestock genetic
evaluation moved from pedigree-and-record systems to genome-wide
markers, before we enter how the genotype matrix is built, how
mixed-model and Bayesian methods consume it, and how the response scale
changes for binary traits.

Selective breeding aims to select animals with better performance for
economically important traits, with breeding value estimates derived
from phenotypic records on the animal and its relatives. Marker data
entered the field gradually through marker-assisted selection (MAS),
then more recently through genomic selection (GS). The 2010s turned GS
into the default evaluation strategy across dairy cattle, beef cattle,
pigs, poultry, crops, and aquaculture. The five sub-pages below trace
that story and place the `masreml` / `masbayes` methods inside it.
